about: Every doctor row and every doctor fix in the order doctor runs them: the one source of ids, order, descriptions and owners (docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/setup-doctor-registry.md section 3). owner is rust:<component> for a row or fix a Rust component judges in the host, or bridge:<step> for one whose layer Node still owns, judged by the bounded Node rows bridge (packages/distribution/contracts/doctor-bridge.v1.json) until that step moves it. repairs names the rows a fix repairs when they do not share its id; a failing row it repairs reports fgos doctor --fix. pointer marks a read-only pointer row. The rows and fixes the config crate lists (packages/config/contracts/doctor-rows.v1.json) enter as one group at their position, with the ids and descriptions this registry gives them.

descriptionOverrides.config-machine-files: the gateway token file ~/.fgos/private/gateway-token exists, is 0600 and holds one line

rows.description: Node >=18 and git available
the running fgOS's own package version and git commit resolve cleanly
shell-integration source line present in detected rc file(s)
a release install has a single fgos on PATH that runs each project's own activated fgos
runner.generatedPaths maps generated sources to render targets with well-formed write-scope entries
project and global runner patterns configuration is present, well-formed, and cumulative
each agent family (providerModel) is served by exactly one executor; its transports are invocations of that executor
every skill an executor declares in supports.skills exists in the skill directory of each CLI the executor invokes, in the main checkout; fails naming the missing path
every family runner.tierFallback lists for a tier has a modelPolicies cell at that tier and an agent executor; warns otherwise
every pool a runner.modelPolicies cell names (model@pool) is declared in runner.llmAccounts, since a pool with no account is skipped by the walk; warns otherwise
runner.llmAccounts is global-only and well formed: pool names without "@" or a family alias, every account with a credentialStore directory per CLI
when runner.llmAccounts is declared, it carries the same accounts and login directories as runner.providers, which the lease still reads for a pool llmAccounts does not declare; warns otherwise
every compiled.json of the running fgOS's domains (the form the Work lifecycle reads) exists, parses, carries the contract this fgOS reads and matches its registry and workflow YAML

agent definition names are unique in the project's own tiers (the workspace tier, and the core tier when the project ships one); a higher tier replaces a lower one whole, and workspace-tier files have the shape the renderer needs; the installed fgOS's own domain and core tiers are judged by npm test

.pi/extensions/fgos-hooks.ts in-process extension enforces dispatch.mjs decide, the decision-question template and the main-checkout delete guard
tool registry posture — inactive/degraded/full

agy sub-HOMEs referenced in executor configs have settings.json configured with toolPermission: always-proceed
curl resolves on PATH (fgctl init downloads releases through it); a missing curl only blocks the download paths
bwrap binary resolves on PATH and minimal smoke test (bwrap --ro-bind / / -- true) exits 0
every open item's risk/kind matches its domain's declared classification vocabulary
every open item sits at a step its own domain's Workflow still registers — no item stranded on a retired step
the Work view holds no recorded cross-machine conflicts: acknowledged changes a concurrent change from another machine kept from applying (warns, never fails)
every fgw/<root> branch is in sync with its real target — no unsynced drift left over from a leaf merge
every live session branch has no post-land drift against its target
every item whose status says its work was handed over has its fgw/<id> branch reachable from the trunk
provider-capacity account leases/quarantine state is reportable; doctor never auto-clears quarantine
the holder-lock driver gives kernel lock exclusion on <fgosDir>/locks and <lockRoot>, proven by a two-process probe on each mount
a lock description borrowed by a git child never leaks to a background process (fgos internal lock-borrow-vectors)
read-only pointer: foreign lock holders, predecessor domains still running and hot records that need a person are read by fgos lock-status
the host binary serves supervise, gate, adopt and attempt-step at protocol 1 and names the containment driver agents run in and its level (kernel or best-effort)
the runtime socket directory exists, is owned by this user and is 0700

read-only pointer: attempts with no closed.json and no lock holder, an attempt whose release was removed named with what to restore; the next fgos run adopts them, or run fgos dispatch recover (a warning, never a failure)
dispatch.gateKillGraceMs and dispatch.cancelWaitMs read through the config door (each at least 1000 ms) and the cancel wait is not shorter than the grace
agent mailbox: whether this project opted in to the mailbox hook rows (mailbox.enabled), and when it did, the record verdict from fgos mailbox status
agent mailbox: whether the Claude Code user settings accept cross-session input (crossSessionInbound), which decides if mail wakes an idle Claude session; report only, fgOS never sets it
agent mailbox: when cross-machine mail is on, an OS timer runs the mailbox sync child every eventStore.sync.intervalSec, so mail is taken on a machine where no session runs a tool

account health: when dispatch.probeAccount.intervalSec is set, an OS timer runs fgos dispatch probe-account --all --record --leg direct every that many seconds, so an exhausted or logged-out account is found between runs; off (0) by default
every capability a core/domain Workflow unit names is declared in runner.capabilities
runner.capabilities' "serves" attribute sets are mutually distinct (I19); the schema states their shape
workerSlots.ceiling is either a positive integer or explicitly null (a malformed value silently enforces nothing)
fgOS Claude Code plugin marketplace is registered and the fgOS plugin is installed/enabled; report only, fgos wire-agents installs it
every operation prompt template in the project tier (.fgos/prompt-templates) validates against bounded variables and schema; the release's domain and core templates are judged by npm test

the terminal-control driver (herdr) answers, which capabilities it declares and which server it talks to, and terminal.* after the config merge with each value and its source; a bad FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE or terminal.* value fails, a missing herdr only warns
terminal slots past allocationGraceMs that never launched and retained panes past their time; reports only, closes nothing

omp's native addon for its installed version is in the natives directory omp resolves (a confined omp cannot extract it); fails only when an executor runs omp, warns when omp is missing or unused; readiness only, no repair
every executor dispatched through a herdr pane names an agent kind herdr can start, and none depends on an outdated herdr integration hook
legacy executor entries hardcoding policy-shaped flags or account-pool-like env, each named with its documented migration target

read-only pointer: confined agent invocations that declare no session directory keep no seat transcript; fgos dispatch probe-session <executorId> shows where the CLI writes it (a warning, never a failure; doctor never runs the probe)
the agent folder-trust store is readable and carries a usable "projects" object, so a dispatch into a fresh worktree can be pre-trusted instead of stopping at a dialog
every confined invocation that reads a login store has an account in the global provider inventory with at least one of that store's credential files, so its agent starts logged in
every executor or invocation declaring a codex-toml or agy/agy-json trustStore reads from a store that is actually readable, the same read a live dispatch will do
the project root is trusted in every codex home and agy sub-HOME the configured executors run under, so a headless dispatch does not stop at a "Trust this folder?" prompt

every seat of every Workflow unit, and every core capability (execute, code:implement, any capability declaring an agent pool) as a writing producer, binds under the committed config in a fixed headless session (no lease, nothing started); a policy refusal or a pool with no executor able to carry the confinement posture fails, no pool, account state, tier caps and shared families are information
every blind Workflow unit can only bind executors whose provider family and transport were proven to keep a worker blind (read-only, no model call)
no executor declares "permissionMode": "bypass" without privateHome, isolatedSession and ownWorktree all true
